description:
Computes travel routes between an origin and a destination, optionally through intermediate stops. Returns the distance and duration for each route.

**Input Requirements (CRITICAL):**

1.  **`origin` and `destination` (objects - MANDATORY):** Each must be provided using exactly one of:
    *   **`address`** (string, e.g., `'Eiffel Tower, Paris'`). Named places, landmarks, and businesses are resolved directly, so do NOT call `search_places` first just to geocode a waypoint. Include any city, region, or country the user mentioned.
    *   **`lat_lng`** (object, `{"latitude": number, "longitude": number}`).
    *   **`place_id`** (string, e.g., `'ChIJOwE_Id1w5EAR4Q27FkL6T_0'`), for example from `search_places`.

2.  **`intermediate_waypoints` (array of objects - OPTIONAL):** Up to 10 stops to pass through, in order, between the origin and destination. Same format as `origin`. Not supported with `TRANSIT`. Only include stops the user asked for.

3.  **`travel_mode` (enum - OPTIONAL):** `DRIVE` (default), `WALK`, `BICYCLE`, or `TRANSIT`.

4.  **Timing (OPTIONAL - set at most ONE):** RFC 3339 timestamps with a UTC offset, e.g., `'2026-09-19T08:00:00-07:00'`. Defaults to departing now. For `TRANSIT`, the time can be up to 7 days in the past or up to 100 days in the future. For other modes, the time can be up to 365 days in the future and must not be in the past.
    *   **`departure_time`:** Use when the user says when they will leave (e.g., "tomorrow at 8am").
    *   **`arrival_time`:** Use when the user says when they must arrive (e.g., "be there by 9am").

5.  **`routing_preference` (enum - OPTIONAL):**
    *   `ROUTING_PREFERENCE_TRAFFIC_UNAWARE` (default): ignores live traffic, incidents, and closures. Lowest latency.
    *   `ROUTING_PREFERENCE_TRAFFIC_AWARE_OPTIMAL`: uses live traffic conditions when available. Not supported for `WALK` or `BICYCLE`. Set this ONLY when the user asks about traffic, congestion, or a traffic-adjusted ETA. It incurs higher cost and latency.

6.  **`location_bias` (object - OPTIONAL):** `{"latitude": number, "longitude": number}` used to disambiguate place names in waypoint addresses. If a name is ambiguous (e.g., "Springfield") and the user gave no region, keep the name as given in `address` and set `location_bias` toward the intended area instead of guessing a region.

7.  **`compute_alternative_routes` (boolean - OPTIONAL):** Set to `true` only when the user asks for route options or alternatives. Defaults to `false`, which returns only the recommended route.

8.  **`include_polyline` (boolean - OPTIONAL):** Set to `true` only when the route geometry (`encoded_polyline`) is needed. Defaults to `false`.

**Instructions for Tool Call:**

*   If the origin or the destination is missing, **you MUST ask the user for clarification** before calling the tool.
*   For "How far is A from B?" questions, use B as the `origin` and A as the `destination`.

**Example Tool Call:**
{"origin":{"address":"Eiffel Tower"},"destination":{"place_id":"ChIJt_5xIthw5EARoJ71mGq7t74"},"intermediate_waypoints":[{"address":"Louvre Museum"}],"travel_mode":"DRIVE","departure_time":"2026-09-19T08:00:00+02:00"}

**Instructions for Response:**

*   When alternative routes are requested, routes are ordered from most to least recommended.
*   If `routes` is empty, tell the user no route was found. Do not guess a route.
*   Only state facts returned by the tool. Do NOT invent turn-by-turn directions, transit lines, stations, platforms, or transfers.
*   The grounded output must be attributed to the source using each route's `attribution` field when available.

LatLng.description: An object that represents a latitude/longitude pair. This is expressed as a pair of doubles to represent degrees latitude and degrees longitude. Unless specified otherwise, this object must conform to the WGS84 standard <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Geodetic_System#1984_version>. Values must be within normalized ranges.

latitude.description: The latitude in degrees. It must be in the range [-90.0, +90.0].

longitude.description: The longitude in degrees. It must be in the range [-180.0, +180.0].

Waypoint.description: Encapsulates a waypoint. Waypoints mark both the beginning and end of a route.

address.description: Human readable address or a plus code. See https://plus.codes for details.

latLng.description: A point specified using geographic coordinates.

placeId.description: The Place ID associated with the waypoint.

arrivalTime.description: Optional. Indicates that the route should be computed based on arrival time.

computeAlternativeRoutes.description: Optional. Whether to compute alternative routes in addition to the recommended route. Defaults to false, in which case only the recommended route is returned. When set to true, up to all available routes are returned, though alternatives may not be available for every request.

departureTime.description: Optional. Indicates that the route should be computed based on departure time.

includePolyline.description: Optional. Whether to include the encoded polyline in the response routes. Defaults to `false`. When set to `true`, `Route.encoded_polyline` is returned.

intermediateWaypoints.description: Optional. Intermediate stops between the origin and destination to pass through in order. At most 10 intermediate waypoints are supported. Intermediate waypoints are not supported when `travel_mode` is `TRANSIT`.

locationBias.description: Optional. A location to bias the search results toward, for example to disambiguate waypoint text queries.

routingPreference.description: Optional. Determines how traffic data is used to compute the route. `ROUTING_PREFERENCE_TRAFFIC_AWARE_OPTIMAL` is not supported when `travel_mode` is `WALK` or `BICYCLE`. For `TRANSIT`, it enables realtime transit data, such as delays and cancellations.
x-google-enum-descriptions: No routing preference specified. Defaults to `ROUTING_PREFERENCE_TRAFFIC_UNAWARE`.
Computes routes without taking live traffic conditions into consideration. Suitable when traffic conditions don't matter or are not applicable. Using this value produces the lowest latency.

Calculates routes taking live traffic conditions into consideration, when traffic data is available. For `TRANSIT`, uses realtime transit data, such as delays and cancellations, when available. This value will trigger the Pro tier and incur higher billing cost and latency. This is only available for allowlisted customers. If not allowlisted, the request will fall back to `ROUTING_PREFERENCE_TRAFFIC_UNAWARE`.

travelMode.description: Optional. Specifies the mode of transportation.
x-google-enum-descriptions: No travel mode specified. Defaults to `DRIVE`.

Travel by walking. NOTE: `WALK` routes are in beta and might sometimes be missing clear sidewalks or pedestrian paths. You must display this warning to the user for all walking that you display in your app.

name: compute_routes

Attribution.description: Required attribution to show with maps content.

title.description: The title to display for the attribution.

url.description: The URL to link to for the attribution.

Route.description: Details about a route between locations.

attribution.description: Required attribution to show with the route.

distanceMeters.description: The travel distance of the route, in meters.

duration.description: The length of time needed to navigate the route.

encodedPolyline.description: An encoded polyline of the route. See https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/utilities/polylinealgorithm

retrievalToken.description: A token that can be used to retrieve this specific route in downstream tools, such as SearchAlongRoute. Valid for 10 minutes.

routes.description: Contains routes between the requested origin and destination, ordered from most recommended to least recommended. Only one route is returned unless `ComputeRoutesRequest.compute_alternative_routes` is set to true.
